_about: Build 2 (3 Nov 2026): lot-side facts. Which edge of a lot faces a street (City street centrelines: vanStreets2026, edmRoads2026), its Edmonton road class, and whether a neighbouring lot is in a residential zone (tile zone codes: vanTax, edmZoningGeo). tool/lotside.js finds them; site.js feeds them into the yards and into which end is the street front. The probe distances in lotside.js are analysis choices, not rules (listed unsourced).

edmResidential._note: Bylaw 20001 table of contents: Part 2 'Residential Zones' (2.10-2.60). Special Area zones named Residential, Row Housing or Apartment (Part 3) are counted as residential zones too: our reading (?). Direct Control zones are not classed (?).

edmIndustrial._note: Bylaw 20001 Part 2 'Industrial Zones' (2.120-2.140); IM 4.1.5-4.1.6 sets setbacks by industrial or non-industrial neighbours

BE._note: s. 2.120 Table 4.1: 4.1.3 abutting streets 6.0 m, 4.1.4 abutting a Collector or Local Road 4.5 m, 4.1.5 abutting sites 0 m, 4.1.6 abutting a site in a residential zone 6.0 m, 4.1.7 alleys 0 m

IM._note: s. 2.130 Table 4.1: 4.1.3 street 3.0 m, 4.1.4 alley 0 m, 4.1.5 abutting a site in a non-industrial zone 6.0 m, 4.1.6 industrial zone 0 m

IH._note: s. 2.140 Table 4.1: 4.1.4 street 3.0 m, 4.1.5 alley or an abutting site 0 m

EIB._note: s. 3.181 Table 5.1: 5.1.3 6.0 m to a street, commercial or residential zone, stormwater facility or private open space corridor; 5.1.4 0 m otherwise (commercial zones not read ?)

EIM._note: s. 3.182 Table 5.1: 5.1.3 street 3.0 m; alley or site 0 m

classes._note: street use or functional class as the City files give it; 'Road' (Edmonton) and leased, recreational or closed streets (Vancouver) carry no class: '?'

vanResidential._note: Vancouver residential districts read from the district names in the tax report's zoning field: our reading (?). Used for the lot-side facts only; no Vancouver yard in the tool depends on it yet.

lines._about: 4 Nov 2026 (LOTLINES brief part 2): which lot line is front, flanking, rear or side, from what it faces (tool/lotside.js classify). Research: checks/research_arch_v1/lotlines.md. The 135 degree corner angle is Edmonton's (s. 8.20 Corner Lot); for Vancouver it is borrowed (our reading ?), as are the 45 degree bands for 'approximately parallel' and 'opposite' in both cities (the complement of 135; no source gives them a number ?).

cornerDeg._note: Corner Lot: 'located at the intersection of 2 Streets, if the angle of the intersection is less than 135 degrees'

frontShortest._note: Vancouver s. 10.26.1(b) and Edmonton s. 8.20 Front Lot Line (b): on a corner, the shorter street line; equal: the Director of Planning (Van 10.26.1(a)) or the Development Planner (Edm 5.130.2) decides

doubleFront._note: Edmonton s. 5.130.4: 'Double Fronting Sites must have 2 Front Lot Lines'. Vancouver: s. 10.26.1 has no rule for a single-lot site on 2 unequal parallel streets (?); s. 10.6.1 Director's approval outside M and I districts

rear._note: Edmonton s. 8.20 Rear Lot Line: 'furthest from and opposite the Front Lot Line'; every other line is an Interior Side Lot Line. Vancouver defines no rear or side property line: the s. 2 yard diagram (F street, S sides, R lane opposite) read the same way (our reading ?); a nearer line facing away (a notch) is unclear there

lane._note: a lane (Van s. 2) or alley (Edm s. 8.20) is not a street, so never a front

vanFlankAsFront._note: on a corner site the exterior side yard is the same as the front yard: I-2 s. 3.2.2.13 (sub-area B), I-3 s. 3.1.2.15, FC-2 ss. 3.1.2.10, 3.2.2.10, 3.3.2.10, 3.4.2.10. I-2 outside sub-area B and I-1C: no such clause found, the flanking line takes the side yard
